annotationRationale: The main route constructs the rotated direction using an isosceles right triangle. Tangent addition provides a distinct trigonometric route. Rotation and the resulting intercept are central; vector coordinates and trigonometric identities remain specific to their respective methods.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate. No subject repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The rotation center lies on the original line. Its direction (5,3) rotates to a direction proportional to (1,4), so the new slope is 4 and the x-intercept is 15, choice B. The stem, choices and key agree; no question figure is supplied or needed.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: AoPS Solution 1 is retained through the midpoint construction, and LIVE/AoPS Solution 2 is retained through tangent addition. AoPS Solution 3 is equivalent trigonometry; Solutions 5 and 7 add rotation machinery without a useful new insight; Solution 6 is a longer angle-bisector calculation. Solution 4 is graphical estimation, and Solution 8 contains a false elimination claim about x=10. No additional route is needed. No shared-bank methods were supplied.
review.annotationCheck: Rotation properties and finding a linear-function intercept are appropriate assessed concepts. Point-slope form is supporting work; coordinate, isosceles-triangle and trigonometric concepts appropriately remain method-specific.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate. No subject repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The quarter-turn sends (5,3) to (-3,5), giving R=(17,25). The midpoint M=(21,24) lies on the internal bisector of the equal perpendicular segments, so PM has exactly the required counterclockwise direction. Its slope is 4, and setting y=0 in the resulting line gives x=15.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The attribution to nonofficial AoPS Solution 1 is accurate. The midpoint construction independently develops its equal-perpendicular-direction idea in original explanatory prose. The source reference and source-informed-original basis are appropriate; no inherited shared provenance is involved.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why finding a direction suffices. The quarter-turn rule, midpoint calculation and isosceles-triangle bisector property make the construction reconstructible without a diagram.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All six immediate nodes fit: rotation properties, vector coordinates, coordinate operations, the isosceles median-bisector property, point-slope form and intercept calculation.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The original inclination satisfies tan(theta)=3/5. Tangent addition has nonzero denominator 2/5 and gives slope 4. The fixed point (20,20) then determines the rotated line and its intercept x=15.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: LIVE and AoPS Solution 2 both supply this argument and are correctly identified as third-party sources. The candidate adds its own motivation and explicit inclination setup; source-informed-original and both reference IDs are appropriate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The connection between rotation, direction angle and slope is explicit. The displayed tangent identity and fixed-center check justify every decisive transition.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: General line form, inclination-based slope, tangent addition, rotation, point-slope form and intercept calculation all occur directly.
